locale.application        composed-default  native-derived         en-US
  ! the application locale this launch presents, on every platform. l10n_util resolves it ahead of every platform candidate -- ahead of glib's LANGUAGE/LC_*/LANG on linux, of NSBundle's preferredLocalizations on macOS, and of both --lang and the Windows preferred-UI-language list on windows -- and LANGUAGE, LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES and LANG are written to it in the browser before the first child is forked, so the C library agrees with ICU and every process agrees with the browser. It decides Intl.DateTimeFormat, NumberFormat and Collator, the calendar and hour cycle they report, the default Accept-Language list, collation order, and Blink's locale-dependent font fallback -- and the rendered width of a <input type=date>, which is how a page reads it with no Intl call at all; no launch layer named a locale, so the composed default is presented rather than the operator's shell
locale.accept_languages   composed-default  native-derived         (the en-US bundle's default)
  ! no launch layer named a list, so no override is composed for locale.accept_languages and the list a page reads is the one the en-US resource bundle declares, which is the list a real user of that locale has -- not the host's, because the application locale is pinned (see locale.application). A single --fingerprint-locale tag, which is what the Python and Node packages pass from GeoIP of the effective egress, names only the application locale; pass a comma-separated list to name the list itself
locale.timezone           host-inherited    host-inherited         (inherited)
  ! no launch layer named locale.timezone, so the host's own is served unchanged and nothing is composed for it. On a direct egress that matches; behind a proxy it is the host's and not the exit's. Pass --fingerprint-timezone to pin it, or launch through the Python or Node package, which resolves it from GeoIP of the effective egress and passes that same switch

limitations
  - anchor macos-metal-apple-850a91233555 is a metal cluster on a swiftshader host: the identity is served as composed, while a method-bearing extension name this host's GL stack lacks is absent from the list
  - anchor macos-metal-apple-850a91233555 serves 44 numeric GL capability limits, composed rather than this host's, to every WebGL context on every backend; the backend underneath may still clamp or refuse an operation taken to one of them, and docs/KNOWN_GAPS.md says which
